content.text: {"candidates":[{"id":"E04","hypothesis_id":"H01","title":"TEA versus TEOA donor-side quenching comparison in the verified P01 baseline matrix","purpose":"Test whether replacing TEOA with TEA changes upstream photoredox observables in a verified P01 baseline formulation under strictly matched nonreactive measurement conditions, as a descriptive covariate for any donor-dependent CO/H2 shift without claiming catalytic causation.","evidence_ids":["EV053","EV065","GX007","EV011"],"source_to_proposal":"EV053 and EV065 support transferable fluorescence/UV-vis quenching logic in donor-containing cobalt photocatalytic systems; GX007 indicates TEA-for-TEOA substitution can alter photochemical behavior; EV011 supports that TEA and TEOA form different donor-derived radical intermediates after quenching. Proposed transfer: use the verified P01 catalytic formulation as the starting matrix, then adapt it only as needed for optical measurement with matched cobalt-containing and cobalt-free references to separate donor-side from cobalt-associated effects. This is proposed characterization, not proof that the same observable controls catalysis.","groups":[{"id":"E04G01","description":"Verified P01 baseline optical sample with TEOA and cobalt A reproducible difference in quenching observable supports donor-dependent upstream photoredox behavior under matched conditions, but not by itself the cause of CO/H2 changes."},{"group_a":"E04G03","group_b":"E04G04","changed_factors":["donor_identity"],"inference":"Single-factor donor comparison without cobalt components. Similar donor ordering here would support an absorber-donor effect that does not require cobalt."},{"group_a":"E04G01","group_b":"E04G03","changed_factors":["cobalt_components"],"inference":"Tests whether cobalt presence alters the optical response in the TEOA matrix, helping bound whether the measured signal includes cobalt-associated pathways."},{"group_a":"E04G02","group_b":"E04G04","changed_factors":["cobalt_components"],"inference":"Tests whether cobalt presence alters the optical response in the TEA matrix, helping bound whether donor dependence changes when cobalt-associated pathways are available."}],"procedure":["First verify the actual P01 baseline composition and prepare matched optical samples that differ only in donor identity or cobalt-component presence across groups.","Record absorber-centered fluorescence and/or UV-vis spectra under identical cuvette geometry, excitation settings, and background subtraction rules, including solvent-only and absorber-free backgrounds when needed.","Use a pilot to adjust optical density into the instrument-linear range and to check whether scattering, adsorption, or donor addition causes unacceptable inner-filter distortion; if so, restrict interpretation to corrected descriptive comparisons or dilute all groups equally.","Compare TEA and TEOA trends first in cobalt-free samples and then in cobalt-containing samples, retaining raw spectra and using Stern-Volmer-style summaries only where empirical linearity is demonstrated."],"measurements":["Steady-state fluorescence intensity of the absorber-containing sample under matched excitation","Optional fluorescence lifetime proxy only if available and if scattering permits meaningful extraction","UV-vis absorbance or difference spectra before and after donor addition or short irradiation exposure","Background absorbance and scattering from donor, solvent matrix, and cobalt-containing mixtures","Empirical quenching trend summaries for cobalt-free and cobalt-containing matrices"],"supports":"A reproducible TEA-versus-TEOA difference in optical quenching or spectral response under otherwise matched conditions, especially if the donor ordering is observed in repeated preparations and survives background correction, supports H01 only in the narrowed sense that donor identity changes upstream photoredox behavior in the verified matrix. If the difference appears only when cobalt components are present, that further supports involvement of cobalt-associated interactions but still does not establish the catalytic mechanism.","refutes":"If TEA and TEOA show no reproducible difference within calibrated detection limits in both cobalt-free and cobalt-containing matched matrices, a large donor-specific upstream optical difference is disfavored as the main explanation for any CO/H2 shift, while leaving downstream proton management, catalyst speciation, and assay artifacts unresolved.","inconclusive":"Results are inconclusive if scattering, adsorption, unstable baselines, donor-dependent decomposition, or noncomparable optical densities prevent reliable matched comparison. A measured optical difference is also inconclusive for catalytic causation unless linked separately to catalytic data.","parameter_selection":"Use the verified P01 baseline identities and nominal component levels as the starting point. Any dilution or path-length adjustment needed for optical work must be applied equally across all groups and documented as an adaptation from the catalytic matrix. Pilot criteria: keep absorbance in an empirically linear instrumental range, avoid complete signal extinction, and accept Stern-Volmer analysis only over the observed linear region; otherwise report matched-point descriptive differences only.","limitations":"This is characterization, not a catalytic readout. In a g-C3N4-containing or otherwise scattering matrix, fluorescence and UV-vis assignments can be compromised by adsorption, inner-filter effects, and turbidity. Even with cobalt-free controls, the experiment cannot identify the turnover-relevant intermediate or prove that a donor-dependent optical change causes a donor-dependent CO/H2 shift. Transfer from EV053, EV065, GX007, and EV011 is methodological and donor-chemistry based, not direct proof for the exact P01 catalytic manifold.","feasibility":"moderate"}]}
